basis: Anal, ear and thumb malformations define the syndrome; renal insufficiency occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and ocular abnormalities are not established as common.
Radioulnar synostosis and radial-ray malformations establish skeletal involvement; unspecified additional malformations cannot support other axes.
Inherited central movement disorder with developmental impairment; reflux and constipation do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Epiphyseal dysplasia causes osteochondral abnormalities and early joint degeneration; no other organ involvement applies across the umbrella.
Congenital structural heart disease defines the group; extracardiac abnormalities vary by syndrome without a shared additional organ.
Corneal edema is an intrinsic corneal disorder; its secondary cause does not establish another affected organ.
Progressive retinal degeneration causes night blindness and eventual visual loss.
Inherited atrial electrical dysfunction; thromboembolic stroke is occasional (5-29%) and a separately diagnosed complication.
Renal dysplasia (12/12) and encephalocele (8/12) define the syndrome; hepatic ductal-plate malformation occurs in 4/5. Documented foot polydactyly is only 1/12.
Tuberculosis directly infects and inflames the peritoneum; pulmonary disease and anemia are not established as common direct involvement.
High-grade glial malignancy originates in the central nervous system.
Airway-esophageal cleft; vertebral malformations 80-99% and cardiac septal defects 30-79%. Motor-neuron anomalies (30-79%) omitted by the four-axis cap.
Self-limited humoral immunodeficiency; infection susceptibility alone does not establish damage to another organ.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 2/2; nystagmus, dental crowding and hirsutism alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Vitamin B6 deficiency with anemia; neuropathy, dermatitis and oral inflammation are possible, but their prevalence is not established at 30% or more.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect; pulmonary arterial hypertension occurs in 2/2 and hepatic injury is supported by elevated transaminases in 2/2 plus hepatomegaly.
Interferon-mediated encephalopathy and leukodystrophy; hepatic disease, cytopenias and skin injury lack an established 30% frequency for this subtype.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is vascular disease; brain injury from rupture or compression is not established as common defining involvement.
Acute malignant proliferation of myeloid cells in blood and marrow; no common qualifying extramedullary organ damage is specified.
Bacterial infection umbrella without a fixed anatomical site; no individual organ is established as affected across most cases.
Inherited high myopia affects 3/3, with retinal detachment in 2/3 and cataract in 1/1; all findings remain within the ocular axis.
Eye, brain and dental defects define syndrome; scoliosis 5/5. Cap omits hypothyroidism (2/3), hearing loss (3/5) and renal calcification (30-79%).
Mitochondrial protein-synthesis defect causes liver failure (13/13); intrinsic coagulation failure, with prolonged prothrombin time in 8/8, supports hematologic involvement.
Neoplasm originates in or occupies the meninges, which belong to the central nervous system.
Hypertension is explicitly cardiovascular despite its pregnancy association; renal, hepatic or neurologic damage is not shared across this umbrella.
